title: Full-Time Measure of a Distance-Learning Term - Questions and Answers on Education Benefits
content:
**Basis Q&A — Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education): the full-time measure that credits of a distance-learning certification are measured against in the rate of pursuit confirmed on a monthly verification.**

**What sets the measure?** The full-time measure of the distance-learning term follows its own length in weeks — the days from its term start to its term end, both counted, divided by 7.

**What are the measures?**
- shorter than 10 weeks: 6 credit hours;
- at least 10 weeks and shorter than 15 weeks: 9 credit hours;
- any other length (15 weeks or longer): the full-time standard of 12 credit hours.

**Is a term of exactly 10 weeks a short term?** No. 70 days is exactly 10 weeks, which is at least 10 weeks, so the measure is 9 credit hours; a 63-day term (9 weeks) is measured against 6.

**Is a term of exactly 15 weeks measured against 9?** No. 105 days is exactly 15 weeks, so the measure is 12 credit hours; a 98-day term (14 weeks) is measured against 9.

**Hypothetical example.** A 7-week distance-learning course of 49 days carrying 3 credits: 3 against a measure of 6 is a half of full time. The same 3 credits in a 16-week distance-learning term are 3 against 12, a quarter of full time.
